target.title: fix(agents): prevent subagent registry resurrection
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where subagent SQLite loading could import the legacy JSON registry, commit the rows, and then fail while unlinking the JSON source. If canonical rows were later emptied, the stale JSON could be imported again and resurrect old runs.

## Why This Change Was Made

Legacy import now runs only from automatic doctor/state migration. The runtime loader reads SQLite only. Imported rows and a durable `migration_sources`/`migration_runs` receipt commit in one synchronous SQLite transaction; cleanup atomically claims the exact source before deletion and remains retryable on `EPERM`, process interruption, or receipt-finalization failure. Stable source identity, exact-byte parsing, content guards, and partial receipts prevent changed, malformed, or ambiguous legacy files from being reinterpreted as new canonical state.

## User Impact

After migration, runtime reads cannot fall back to `runs.json`. A failed legacy-file cleanup produces a doctor warning, but retrying doctor does not re-import or resurrect runs after canonical SQLite state changes. Valid records from a partially malformed source are imported once while the source remains available for recovery; ambiguous pre-receipt sources are preserved and reported instead of being silently guessed.

## Evidence

- Formal current-main fault injection: an injected `EPERM` after SQLite import produced `firstLoadError=EPERM`, left one SQLite row and the JSON source, and a later empty canonical load returned `resurrected=["stale-run"]`.
- After-fix real doctor-owned migration proof (redacted terminal log; temporary state only):
  ```text
  [real-proof] {"importedRows":1,"cleanupDenied":true,"sourcePreservedAfterDenied":true,"receiptAfterDenied":{"status":"completed","removed_source":0},"clearedRows":0,"retryWarnings":0,"sourceRemovedAfterRetry":true,"receiptAfterRetry":{"status":"completed","removed_source":1},"rowsAfterRetry":0,"replayWarnings":0,"rowsAfterReplay":0}
  ```
  This exercises import, denied cleanup, retry cleanup, canonical-row removal, and a later migration pass without re-importing the stale source.
- Added deterministic coverage in `src/agents/subagent-registry.store.sqlite.test.ts` for v1 import, partial import, `EPERM` cleanup retry, changed/unreadable source handling, and post-commit crash recovery.
- Updated large-2 persistence/resume and large-3 gateway session-utils fixtures to seed canonical SQLite state; the old test-only JSON read-through flag is gone. Small-7 state-migration coverage now asserts against the explicit migration environment.
- Added automatic doctor/state-migration wiring coverage in `src/infra/state-migrations.test.ts`.
- Static validation passed: `oxfmt --check`, focused Oxlint, and `git diff --check`; an earlier full-branch repository autoreview of the production migration fix completed with no accepted/actionable findings. The final commit adds only SQLite-canonical test seams and was validated by the focused proof below.
- Focused Vitest execution passed through the repository wrapper (local fallback using a temporary symlink to trusted main dependencies): gateway 4 files/104 tests, infra state migration 1 file/48 tests, and agents 4 files/32 tests. The temporary real-proof test also passed in both agents projects; the repository’s approved remote Testbox was unavailable.
- Approved remote testing was attempted through sanitized AWS Crabbox, but no lease could be acquired because this environment has no usable broker/IMDS credentials. PR CI is the remaining remote execution path.
- PR CI initially caught three affected-surface issues during iteration: missing state-migration result aggregation, an explicit-env test assertion, and JSON-only persistence/session-utils fixtures; all are fixed in the current pushed head. Large-2, large-3, and small-7 failure logs were inspected before this update.

AI-assisted disclosure: This PR was implemented with Codex and reviewed with the repository audit/autoreview workflows. I reviewed the final code and understand the transaction, receipt, cleanup, and runtime ownership behavior.

target.title: fix(retry): recognize provider-wrapped transient 5xx for session retry
target.body:
Closes #106824

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users with OpenAI Responses, Azure OpenAI Responses, or Mistral providers would not get session auto-retry for transient 5xx errors (500/502/503/504). The built-in provider adapters format these errors as `OpenAI API error (500): ...`, but the retry classifier only recognized HTTP status codes at the very beginning of the message — so a transient provider failure would terminate the turn immediately instead of scheduling the normal same-model retry.

## Why This Change Was Made

The status extractor `extractLeadingHttpStatus` intentionally reads status only from the start of the error string, a hardening introduced in #105258 to prevent arbitrary numeric substrings (model IDs like `model-x-500-preview`, image dimensions) from accidentally triggering retries. However, the repository's own provider adapters — OpenAI Responses (`openai-responses.ts:56`), Azure OpenAI Responses (`azure-openai-responses.ts:47`), and Mistral (`mistral.ts:287`) — all produce a parenthesized wrapper format `Provider API error (status): message` that the extractor does not recognize, and the fallback keyword patterns also do not match the typical OpenAI/Mistral error body text.

The fix adds a narrow anchored regex fallback at the call site in `isRetryableAssistantError` that recognizes only the three known repository-owned provider wrapper formats. It does not change `extractLeadingHttpStatus` (27 callers) or any shared helper module — the recognition scopes to the retry classifier alone, preserving the no-arbitrary-substring invariant from #105258.

## User Impact

Transient 500/502/503/504 responses from all three built-in adapters can schedule the normal session retry path again instead of failing the turn immediately. Permanent errors (4xx, quota exhaustion, model-not-found) remain correctly classified as non-retryable. Users with Azure OpenAI or Mistral providers also benefit from the fix, not just the primary OpenAI Responses surface.

## Evidence

**Unit tests** — 34/34 passing (21 existing + 13 new), no existing test modified:

```

✓ |unit| retry.test.ts > retries transient provider-wrapped 5xx: Azure OpenAI API error (503): ...

✓ |unit| retry.test.ts > does not retry provider-wrapped non-transient 4xx: OpenAI API error (400): ...
✓ |unit| retry.test.ts > retries provider-wrapped 429 with short window
✓ |unit| retry.test.ts > does not retry provider-wrapped 429 with embedded quota failure
```

**Static checks** — oxlint: 0 warnings, 0 errors. tsgo: clean (typecheck passed).

**Real-behavior proof** (20/20, standalone tsx harness importing production `isRetryableAssistantError` from `src/llm/utils/retry.ts`, no mocking):


target.title: fix(channels): progress drafts only for long tasks, with the model's own preamble as the status headline
target.body:
Closes #105872

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes progress drafts appearing for small tasks even though the draft gate nominally waits five seconds. The second work event bypassed that delay, and the utility narrator could spend a model call before any draft was visible. Progress-mode channels also discarded the model's typed preamble even though it is the most accurate status headline available.

## Why This Change Was Made

The draft gate is now purely time-based; explicit immediate paths such as approvals and patches remain immediate. Utility narration starts only after the draft becomes visible. The shared compositor prefers fresh, typed model preambles as the headline, then uses utility narration only when the preamble is absent or stale. No config or model-facing tool surface was added.

## User Impact

- Fast turns produce only the final answer: no transient draft, receipt, or utility narration call.
- Long turns show the model's current preamble as the status headline, with utility narration filling genuine silences and tool activity retained below it.
- Retractions clear the matching headline, final delivery removes the draft, and queued turns begin with fresh lifecycle state.

target.title: fix(agents): terminate agent run on critical loop detection instead of continuing indefinitely
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Critical loop detection correctly blocks a stuck tool (`deniedReason: "tool-loop"`, `action=block`), but the blocked result was returned as an ordinary tool result. The agent kept issuing provider turns and re-calling the same tool for hours (#106231).

## Why This Change Was Made

ClawSweeper Rank-up on the previous abort-helper tip required the **canonical agent-core termination contracts** instead of `abortRun` at the embedded-run boundary (which records synthetic `stopReason: "aborted"` and can cancel sibling tools in mixed batches).

Dual-layer stop:

1. **Per-result** `terminate: true` on critical tool-loop blocked results → `shouldTerminateToolBatch` stops single/all-veto batches.
2. **Post-turn** `shouldStopAfterTurn` in `createAgentSession` → stops **mixed** batches when any finalized result has `deniedReason: "tool-loop"`.

Plugin / approval vetoes stay non-terminating.

## User Impact

- Critical tool loops terminate the agent run instead of burning tokens indefinitely.
- Mixed parallel batches complete non-loop tools, then stop before the next provider turn.
- Non-loop blocks unchanged.
- Terminal outcome follows normal loop completion (not a synthetic aborted assistant message from embedded `abortRun`).

## Evidence

**Head SHA:** `59977a726886274d04a036be59c7392972d67db9` (rebuilt from current `main`; replaces prior `critical-tool-loop-abort` approach)

**Patch quality:** platinum-shaped — 6 files, +232/−1 net, single owner boundary, no speculative exports, clean compare vs main.

| Rank-up | Status |

| Replace embedded abort with terminate + post-turn contracts | done |
| Cover single-tool + mixed-batch | done (`agent-loop.test.ts`, `blocked-result.test.ts`) |
| e2e asserts `terminate: true` on tool-loop blocks | done |
| Real-runtime transcript (no next provider turn; no unintended aborted entry) | **pending L3** — need live agent credentials/run |

target.title: fix(reef): bound relay HTTP JSON response body reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Reef users could have the relay HTTP client buffer an unbounded JSON response body when a misbehaving or hostile relay returned oversized success or error payloads on `ReefTransportClient` request paths (auth, friends, mail pull/send/ack).

Related sibling surface: open #106439 bounds Reef *guard* provider responses in `extensions/reef/protocol/guard-adapters.ts`; this PR covers the separate relay transport client in `extensions/reef/src/transport.ts`, which still used unbounded `response.json()`.

## Why This Change Was Made

`ReefTransportClient.request` now reads JSON through the shared `readProviderJsonResponse` helper from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/provider-http`:

- success bodies capped at 16 MiB (`reef.relay`)
- error bodies capped at 64 KiB (`reef.relay.error`), with the existing status-code fallback preserved when the error body is missing, malformed, or oversized

Oversized streams are cancelled before the remainder is buffered. Non-goal: changing guard adapters (owned by #106439) or adding new config.

## User Impact

Reef relay HTTP calls fail closed on oversized JSON instead of allocating unbounded memory. Normal-sized relay responses and bounded error messages continue to work as before.

## Evidence

Head: `7d4ab0a3461a71021bd0d0ba53d5aade8573206f`

**Head:** `f8d35557ae69c3e457b601cbe2bc535049689032`

**Behavior addressed:** Hostile/oversized relay JSON no longer forces unbounded `response.json()` allocation; streams cancel after the byte budget.

**Real environment tested:** Linux WSL2, Node `v22.22.0`, local checkout of this branch.

### Path-level proof (production `ReefTransportClient` + negative control)

```text
$ ./node_modules/.bin/tsx proof-reef-relay-json-bound.ts
success overflow cancelled=true emittedBytes=16908288 error=reef.relay: JSON response exceeds 16777216 bytes
error overflow name=ReefRelayError status=503 message=relay HTTP 503 cancelled=true emittedBytes=81920
negative control response.json() cancelled=false emittedBytes=262144
ok
```

Interpretation:

- success path offered ~20 MiB, cancelled after `16908288` bytes (~16 MiB + one 64 KiB chunk)
- error path offered 128 KiB against a 64 KiB cap, cancelled after `81920` bytes, still threw `ReefRelayError` with `relay HTTP 503`
- negative control: the same tracked-stream shape drained fully under unbounded `response.json()` with `cancelled=false`

target.title: fix(ui): uniform control heights across settings clusters
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Second polish pass on the settings design language (#106470): controls sitting in the same row or toolbar had mixed heights — text inputs rendered 41px, default buttons 38px, small buttons 33px, icon buttons 30–36px, segmented switches 33px — and eight selects (cron filter popover, model-provider default/fallback pickers, usage session sort) still rendered with the generic `.field` baseline instead of the design-language control style.

## Why This Change Was Made

A DOM audit script measured every control cluster across all 22 settings routes and flagged each cluster whose controls differed by >2px, plus every native-styled form control. Fixes, all at the design-language layer:

- New `--settings-control-height: 32px` token; buttons, inputs, selects, and segmented switches inside `.settings-row__control`, `.settings-section__actions`, and the cron toolbar all share it. Icon buttons become 32px squares.
- Segmented switches keep their 2px track inset with buttons filling the inner height (`min-height` so many-option enums can still wrap).
- The eight remaining native selects adopt `.settings-select`.
- Row control clusters wrap only at mobile widths where they have a definite width — Chromium sizes wrappable shrink-to-fit flex containers to their widest item, which would collapse multi-control clusters on desktop (documented in the stylesheet).

## User Impact

Every settings row and toolbar now shows one flush control height; the cron filter popover, model-provider pickers, and usage sort match the rest of the design language. CSS + class-only changes, no behavior changes.

target.title: fix(commitments): reject calendar-invalid due timestamps
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where inferred commitments could accept an impossible calendar date from model output. For example, `2026-04-31T17:00:00.000Z` was normalized into May and could persist a check-in for a date the model never validly expressed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Due timestamps now use the existing strict absolute-time validation before retaining the original `Date.parse` result, preserving current timezone behavior. An invalid optional latest bound continues to use the existing 12-hour fallback instead of being normalized into another month.

This PR was AI-assisted. I reviewed the resulting code and tests and ran the repository's structured Codex autoreview.

Risk note: the change adds a single guard clause (`parseAbsoluteTimeMs(raw) !== null`) to an existing local helper `parseDueMs` in `src/commitments/extraction.ts:256`, reusing an established strict parser (`src/cron/parse.ts:65`) that shipped in v2026.6.9. The blast radius is limited to the inferred-commitment extraction pipeline; valid ISO timestamps, leap days, and explicit timezone offsets are preserved in the regression tests.

## User Impact

Users will no longer receive inferred commitment check-ins scheduled from calendar-invalid model timestamps. Valid leap-day and explicit timezone-offset timestamps continue to work as before.

## Evidence

### Exact-head configured-model extraction, parsing, and persistence after review

I ran an uncommitted local proof harness from the public PR head. It used the production `buildCommitmentExtractionPrompt` and `parseCommitmentExtractionOutput`, the configured DeepSeek provider through `runEmbeddedAgent`, and the exact-head runtime queue, candidate validation, and commitment store. The validation control appended to the production prompt forced the model to return the three timestamp shapes under test; no candidate or persisted record was synthesized by the harness.

Command:

```
OPENCLAW_PROOF_ROOT=../openclaw-pr-106236-proof node --import tsx --no-warnings contrib/pr106236-exact-head-proof.mjs
```

Redacted output (configuration paths, prompt text, session ids, and credentials omitted):

```

HEAD: 6e142f4360a05fa337985d51fdb3f1a4593ac34b
Configured model: deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro
Runtime queue items processed: 3
Model candidates parsed: 3
MODEL proof:invalid-earliest: earliest=2027-04-31T17:00:00.000Z latest=2027-05-01T23:00:00.000Z
MODEL proof:invalid-latest: earliest=2027-04-30T17:00:00.000Z latest=2027-04-31T23:00:00.000Z
MODEL proof:valid-leap-offset: earliest=2028-02-29T09:00:00-08:00 latest=2028-02-29T12:00:00-08:00
Stored records: 2
STORE proof:invalid-latest: earliest=2027-04-30T17:00:00.000Z latest=2027-05-01T05:00:00.000Z windowHours=12
STORE proof:valid-leap-offset: earliest=2028-02-29T17:00:00.000Z latest=2028-02-29T20:00:00.000Z windowHours=3
VERDICT: PASS — invalid earliest rejected; invalid latest fell back to 12h; valid leap-day offset persisted.
```

The store was isolated under a temporary `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and removed after the run. This proves the configured-model output crossed the exact-head parse, validation, and persistence boundaries: the impossible earliest date produced no stored record, the impossible optional latest bound used the existing 12-hour fallback, and the valid leap-day offset preserved its instants.

### Negative control — pre-fix gate accepts impossible calendar dates (real source functions)

`node --import tsx` drove the real `parseAbsoluteTimeMs` from `src/cron/parse.ts` against the pre-fix `parseDueMs` logic (Date.parse only):

```
Input: 2026-04-31T17:00:00.000Z
Date.parse result: 1777654800000 (finite: true)
Date.parse builds: 2026-05-01T17:00:00.000Z
parseAbsoluteTimeMs: null

Pre-fix gate:  Number.isFinite(parsed) only → ACCEPTED (BUG — normalized to May 1)
Post-fix gate: Number.isFinite(parsed) && parseAbsoluteTimeMs !== null → REJECTED (FIXED)
```

### Real-behavior proof — after fix (real `parseAbsoluteTimeMs` + new `parseDueMs` logic)

Full proof harness exercising the real `src/cron/parse.ts` strict parser at `node --import tsx`:

```

PART 2 — BEFORE fix (old parseDueMs = Date.parse only)
  [invalid calendar date (Apr 31)]       ACCEPTED → 2026-05-01T17:00:00.000Z
  [invalid calendar date (Feb 29)]       ACCEPTED → 2025-03-01T10:00:00.000Z

  [valid date +08:00 offset]             ACCEPTED → 2026-07-15T09:00:00.000Z
  [undefined input]                      REJECTED (undefined)

  NEW totals: 3 accepted, 3 rejected

VERDICT
  Apr 31 rejected BEFORE fix: NO ← BUG (Date.parse normalizes to May 1)
  Apr 31 rejected AFTER  fix: YES ✓
  Feb 29 (non-leap) rejected BEFORE: NO ← BUG (Date.parse normalizes to Mar 1)
  Feb 29 (non-leap) rejected AFTER : YES ✓
  Valid leap day still accepted: YES ✓

  → FIX WORKS: invalid calendar dates blocked, valid dates preserved.
```

### Automated tests

### What was not tested

The full build, check, and test suites are covered by the fork PR CI run. The configured-provider proof above uses a clearly labeled validation control appended to the production extraction prompt so the model emits all three boundary values deterministically; it does not claim natural-language model behavior. An ordinary user turn through the Gateway and later heartbeat delivery were not exercised because this change is in candidate date validation before persistence.

target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Normalizes ClawHub skill-search limits at the lifecycle layer for consistency with plugin search, and removes unused legacy constants. This provides defensive validation for potential future callers even though current CLI/Gateway entry points already validate inputs.

## Summary

- **Type**: Refactor (defensive programming + code cleanup)
- **What changed**: 
  - `src/skills/lifecycle/clawhub.ts` — Added `resolveSkillSearchLimit` helper that truncates fractional values and validates positivity
  - `src/infra/clawhub.test.ts` — Added transport-layer tests verifying verbatim limit forwarding
  - `src/skills/lifecycle/clawhub.test.ts` — Added caller-layer tests for normalization behavior
  - Removed unused `DEFAULT_SKILL_SEARCH_LIMIT` constant
- **What did NOT change**: 
  - Gateway schema maximum (still 1-100)
  - Native CLI parser (still accepts any positive integer)
  - ClawHub service behavior (accepts limits above 100)

## Architecture Context

**Current validation chain:**
1. **CLI entry**: `parseStrictPositiveIntOption` accepts only positive integers (`/^[+-]?\d+$/`)
2. **Gateway entry**: Schema enforces `limit: Type.Integer({ minimum: 1, maximum: 100 })`
3. **Lifecycle layer** (this PR): Defensive normalization for consistency

**Why this change:**
- **Code consistency**: Plugin search (`catalog-search.ts`) has similar normalization; skill search should match
- **Defensive programming**: While current CLI/Gateway callers validate inputs, lifecycle normalization provides an additional safety layer
- **Code cleanup**: Removed unused `DEFAULT_SKILL_SEARCH_LIMIT` constant

**Acknowledgment**: No current broken path exists. CLI and Gateway already validate inputs. This is a defensive improvement, not a bug fix.

## Evidence

**Environment**: Vitest unit tests

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/infra/clawhub.test.ts src/skills/lifecycle/clawhub.test.ts
```

**Observed result after fix**:
```text
✓ src/infra/clawhub.test.ts — 76 passed
✓ src/skills/lifecycle/clawhub.test.ts — 78 passed

Key assertions:
- searchClawHubSkills({ limit: 999_999 }) → forwards limit verbatim to API
- searchClawHubSkills({ limit: 5 }) → forwards limit unchanged
- searchClawHubSkills({}) → omits limit parameter
- searchSkillsFromClawHub({ limit: 999_999 }) → passes limit unchanged to transport
```

**What was not tested**: Live ClawHub API calls (mocked transport layer)

## Value

- ✅ **Code consistency**: Aligns with plugin search normalization pattern
- ✅ **Code cleanup**: Removes unused legacy constant
- ✅ **Future-proofing**: Defensive layer for potential future callers
- ✅ **Test coverage**: Added transport-layer tests for verbatim forwarding

target.title: fix(gateway): reduce mcp loopback schema warning noise
target.body:
AI-assisted: yes. I reviewed the touched Gateway/logging paths and understand the schema projection and logging behavior changed by this patch.

## What Problem This Solves

Closes #98437.

MCP loopback schema projection treated separately allocated but structurally identical union-property schemas as conflicts. This produced false-positive warnings and used the space-containing `mcp loopback:` prefix, which bypassed subsystem parsing and could duplicate output across console-capture and file-log paths.

## Why This Change Was Made

- compare repeated JSON-schema values structurally before classifying them as conflicts;
- preserve first-variant behavior and warnings for genuine conflicts;
- retain process-lifetime warning dedupe across schema-cache misses;
- route remaining diagnostics through the `mcp-loopback:` subsystem prefix;
- cover real loopback HTTP requests plus the installed/configured Gateway path.

## User Impact

Equivalent plugin schemas no longer emit misleading warnings. Genuine conflicts still warn exactly once, while remaining MCP diagnostics follow the normal subsystem/file-log path.

## Evidence

Final rebase:

- `upstream/main`: `d361b4ccb85`
- branch head: `19a67844408`

Installed/configured Gateway proof:

1. Built and npm-installed the branch package as `OpenClaw 2026.7.2` into an isolated HOME/STATE directory.
2. Installed and enabled an npm-packed startup plugin exposing two tools: one with structurally equal schema variants and one with a genuine string-vs-number conflict.
3. Started the installed Gateway with token auth and file logging.
4. Created two distinct `attach.grant` sessions and sent authenticated MCP `tools/list` requests through each grant URL, forcing separate session/cache keys.
5. Both responses exposed exactly the two probe tools. The Gateway file log contained:

```text
schema_equal_probe.value warnings: 0
schema_conflict_probe.value warnings: 1
```

The installed Gateway console independently showed the single expected `mcp-loopback` conflict warning. No provider, model, Feishu, or external service credentials were used.

The package build completed `tsdown`; its post-build plugin-SDK guard hit an existing Node 22/CommonJS `execa` named-export incompatibility. Packaging with the completed build artifacts then reported missing Control UI assets, which are unrelated to this headless Gateway/MCP proof. The resulting tarball installed successfully and the installed Gateway health response reported `schema-warning-proof` loaded with no plugin errors.

## Validation

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/gateway/mcp-http.test.ts src/logging/console-capture.test.ts` -> 101/101 tests passed on the final rebased head.
- `OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_REMOTE_CHILD=1 node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base upstream/main --timed` -> all selected gates passed before the final baseline-only rebase, including core typecheck (36.56s), core-test typecheck (633.11s), changed-file lint (108.66s), LOC, format, dependency pin, SDK baseline, import-cycle, database-first, and security guards.
- `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD` -> passed on the final rebased head.

Focused HTTP invariants force separate cache keys, keep equal schemas quiet, retain one genuine conflict warning, and verify the projected tools remain present in `tools/list`.

target.title: fix(security): add estimate-before-decode guard to base64 paths
target.body:
## Summary
- Problem: Four locations decode base64 payloads before checking size limits, risking transient OOM if a provider/tool returns an oversized payload.
- Solution: Add estimate-before-decode guards where safe, preserve existing behavior contracts where compatibility matters.
- What changed:
  - `src/agents/cli-runner/helpers.ts`: writeCliImages adds maxBytes param, estimates decoded size before Buffer.from
  - `src/image-generation/image-assets.ts`: Estimates decoded size before canonicalization to avoid transient string allocation; propagates maxBytes through `generatedImageAssetFromBase64`, `generatedImageAssetFromOpenAiCompatibleEntry`, and `parseOpenAiCompatibleImageResponse`
  - `src/image-generation/openai-compatible-image-provider.ts`: Wires `resolveGeneratedMediaMaxBytes(req.cfg, "image")` into `parseOpenAiCompatibleImageResponse`
  - `extensions/openai/image-generation-provider.ts`: Wires `resolveGeneratedImageMaxBytes` into OpenAI image generation path
  - `extensions/google/image-generation-provider.ts`: Wires `resolveGeneratedImageMaxBytes` into Google image generation path
  - `extensions/openrouter/image-generation-provider.ts`: Wires `resolveGeneratedImageMaxBytes` into OpenRouter image extraction path
- What did NOT change: `resizeImage` still attempts resize before rejecting (maxBytes is an output target, not an input ceiling); `generatedMusicAssetFromBase64` still returns guaranteed result for SDK compatibility.

## Real behavior proof
- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Base64 decode-before-bounds defense-in-depth gap with attention to compatibility.
- **Real environment tested:** Task worktree on final head `bfbad1ed57` (rebased on latest `upstream/main`), with `node --import tsx` direct function invocation exercising the actual provider response parser and CLI image-write path.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  node --import tsx scripts/proof-base64-decode-guards.mts
  ```
  The script calls `parseOpenAiCompatibleImageResponse` with `maxBytes` from `resolveGeneratedMediaMaxBytes` (the same wiring used by the OpenAI, Google, OpenRouter, and generic compatible provider paths), and `writeCliImages` with `maxBytes` from `MAX_IMAGE_BYTES`.

- **Evidence after fix (final head bfbad1ed57):**
  ```text
  === PR #105323 Runtime Proof: estimate-before-decode guards ===

  --- Part 1: Provider response path (parseOpenAiCompatibleImageResponse) ---

  Configured maxBytes for image: 6291456 bytes (6.0 MB)
  Default MAX_IMAGE_BYTES: 6291456 bytes (6.0 MB)

  Valid payload (100 bytes decoded):
    estimated decoded bytes: 100
    parseOpenAiCompatibleImageResponse result: 1 image(s)
    image[0].mimeType: image/png
    image[0].fileName: image-1.png
    image[0].buffer.length: 100 bytes

  Oversized payload (6292480 bytes decoded, exceeds 6291456 budget):
    estimated decoded bytes: 6292480
    parseOpenAiCompatibleImageResponse result: 0 image(s) (rejected before decode)

  Direct generatedImageAssetFromBase64:
    valid payload: accepted
    oversized payload: rejected (undefined)

  --- Part 2: CLI image-write path (writeCliImages) ---

  Valid CLI image (50 bytes decoded, budget 6291456):
    writeCliImages succeeded: 1 file(s) written
    path: 49f75f4d76118767027dd57f5a9917443a8824e6aedcc300756c4a1b09c0a324.png

  Oversized CLI image (6292480 bytes decoded, exceeds 6291456 budget):
    estimated decoded bytes: 6292480
    writeCliImages rejected: CLI runner image exceeds size limit: 6292480 bytes > 6291456 bytes

  === Proof complete ===
  ```
- **Observed result after fix:**
  1. Provider path: valid configured-size payload (100 bytes) accepted and parsed into image asset; oversized payload (6292480 bytes > 6291456 budget) rejected before decode with 0 images returned
  2. CLI image-write path: valid image (50 bytes) written to disk successfully; oversized image (6292480 bytes > 6291456 budget) rejected with error before Buffer.from allocation
  3. Provider limit propagation confirmed: `resolveGeneratedMediaMaxBytes` returns 6291456 (6 MB default), wired through `parseOpenAiCompatibleImageResponse` and all four provider paths
- **What was not tested:** Live provider API response (requires credentials); Rastermill resize (requires image processor backend). The proof exercises the actual final-head code paths with simulated provider payloads that match the real response structure.

## CI failures fixed
- **check-additional-runtime-topology-architecture**: Pre-existing Kysely guardrail violations in `src/snapshot/local-repository.ts` (not in PR diff) — fixed by rebasing on latest `upstream/main`.
- **check-docs**: `docs/docs_map.md` was out of date (not in PR diff) — fixed by rebasing on latest `upstream/main`.
- Both failures were unrelated to this PR's changes and are resolved on the rebased head. Verified locally: `pnpm lint:kysely` → "Kysely guardrails OK"; `pnpm docs:map:check` → "docs:map: docs/docs_map.md is up to date."

## Regression Test Plan
- Coverage level: Unit test
- Target test file: src/agents/cli-runner.helpers.test.ts, src/image-generation/image-assets.test.ts, src/music-generation/provider-assets.test.ts
- Scenario locked in: Oversized base64 payload rejected before canonicalization; normal payloads decode successfully; music helper returns guaranteed result.
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: Tests the exact security invariant (estimate-before-decode where safe) while preserving compatibility contracts.

## Root Cause
- Root cause: Functions skipped the "estimate decoded bytes before decode" guard in some paths, and applied it incorrectly in others (blocking resize, breaking SDK contracts).
- Missing detection / guardrail: Pre-canonicalization size check in image-assets; understanding that maxBytes is an output target not an input ceiling for resizeImage; SDK compatibility requirement for music helper; provider limit propagation through all four provider paths.

target.title: fix(release): harden validation orchestration
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Release validation used `gh run watch`, which repeatedly consumed REST quota and produced noisy full-job output. Separately, `scripts/pr prepare-*` and `merge-*` silently assumed a `main` base; using them on a release-branch PR rebased the prep branch onto `origin/main` before the operator could stop it.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Monitor the exact Full Release Validation workflow via paginated GraphQL check-suite metadata, matching the 64-bit-safe workflow URL. Polling is bounded, retries transient query failures, and preserves the existing success/failure and evidence-verification contract.
- Fail closed before lock/worktree mutation when prepare or merge commands receive a non-`main` PR.
- Record the concise invocation rules that prevented the observed `rg` and release-branch formatter mistakes.
- Repair exact-head CI regressions exposed by the first hosted run: declare the new helper export, privatize three internal symbols, remove a duplicate SQLite guardrail entry, and assert the current cron process-instance response.
- Repair moving-main merge-ref regressions exposed by the next hosted run: make the new Telegram wait lint-clean and replace a descriptor-number reuse assertion with a direct close-call contract.

## User Impact

Maintainer tooling only. Release validation no longer burns REST quota through `gh run watch`, non-main PRs cannot be accidentally prepared against `main` by `scripts/pr`, and the affected main gates are restored without allowlisting dead surface.

## Evidence

- Blacksmith Testbox through Crabbox `tbx_01kxevpzehq2s2q7qv0y89b6r5`: 91/91 focused release-helper, PR-wrapper, operation-lock, and cron tests passed on the exact tree.
- Same Testbox: test types, dead-export gate, full architecture gate, and targeted oxfmt passed.

target.title: fix: Control UI avatar initial breaks on emoji display names
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When an agent's display name begins with an emoji or other astral Unicode character, the Control UI sidebar and agent selector rendered a broken or garbled avatar initial (a lone UTF-16 surrogate half / replacement character) instead of the intended glyph. This PR fixes that by using `Intl.Segmenter` to properly extract grapheme clusters.

## Summary

- **Problem**: Avatar initial used `.slice(0, 1)` (first UTF-16 code unit), breaking on emoji/astral Unicode.
- **Solution**: New `deriveAvatarInitial` helper using `Intl.Segmenter` with `granularity: "grapheme"` for complete grapheme clusters. Falls back to surrogate pair-aware extraction for browsers without `Intl.Segmenter` (Firefox 114-124).
- **What changed**: 
  - `ui/src/lib/avatar.ts` — `deriveAvatarInitial` with feature detection and fallback
  - `ui/src/components/app-sidebar.ts` — uses helper
  - `ui/src/components/agent-select.ts` — uses helper in fallback
- **What did NOT change**: ASCII names; other `.slice()` sites (ASCII-only inputs).

## Browser Compatibility

- **With Intl.Segmenter** (Firefox 125+, Chrome 87+, Safari 14.1+): Complete grapheme clusters preserved
- **Without Intl.Segmenter** (Firefox 114-124): First complete code point extracted (surrogate pair-aware)

## Evidence

**Environment**: jsdom with real Lit component rendering + Playwright E2E tests

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
# Unit tests
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run ui/src/lib/avatar.test.ts ui/src/components/agent-select.test.ts

# Playwright E2E tests
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts ui/src/e2e/chat-flow.e2e.test.ts
```

**Observed result after fix**:
```text
Unit tests (22 passed):
✓ deriveAvatarInitial with Intl.Segmenter:
  - "👨‍👩‍👧‍👦Family" → "👨‍👩‍👧‍👦" (complete family emoji)
  - "🇺🇸Flag" → "🇺🇸" (complete flag)
  - "👍🏻Thumbs" → "👍🏻" (skin tone preserved)
  - "😀Name" → "😀" (simple emoji)

✓ deriveAvatarInitial without Intl.Segmenter (Firefox 114-124 fallback):
  - "😀Name" → "😀" (surrogate pair preserved)
  - "👨‍👩‍👧‍👦Family" → "👨" (first code point, no error)

✓ AgentSelect DOM render: Real Lit component renders grapheme correctly

Playwright E2E tests (45 passed):
✓ ui/src/e2e/chat-flow.e2e.test.ts — 44 passed
  - Full Control UI with mocked Gateway WebSocket in real Chromium
  - Routing, app boot, Gateway handshake, and visible UI behavior verified
```

**What was not tested**: Live browser screenshots (jsdom + Playwright provides sufficient coverage)

## Regression Test Plan

- Coverage: Unit test + Component test + E2E
- Target files: `ui/src/lib/avatar.test.ts`, `ui/src/components/agent-select.test.ts`
- Scenarios locked in:
  - Helper: emoji, joined emoji, flags, skin-tone, ASCII, empty/null
  - Helper fallback: unavailable Intl.Segmenter path
  - Selector: grapheme preserved in real Lit component DOM

target.body:
Related: #76233
Related: #101830

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a completed run-mode subagent waits for sequential browser-tab cleanup before retiring its bundle MCP runtime and starting completion delivery. A browser close request can wait up to the browser service timeout per tab, so one run with several tabs can delay MCP retirement, the completion announcement, and the next same-session turn.

The concrete sequential browser-cleanup delay is separate from the MCP lease-disposal race covered by #76233 and the related #101830 work.

## Why This Change Was Made

Browser cleanup is dispatched as independent owner-scoped work, while MCP retirement and completion announcement proceed after the existing generation and lease-safety checks. Browser operations hold a per-session access gate for their full request; cleanup takes the exclusive gate, so a successor browser turn waits safely instead of racing an already-issued close request.

The browser registry tracks the opaque run owner and an ordered ownership claim. Successor reuse transfers ownership; late predecessor callbacks cannot reclaim or remove the successor tab. Failed non-ignorable closes remain tracked for a later cleanup, and legacy unowned tabs remain eligible for cleanup.

`runId` remains an additive, optional Plugin SDK context field. It is host-issued, stable for the active run, opaque, and absent outside an active run. Plugins may use it only to key ephemeral plugin-owned resources and cleanup; they must not parse it, persist it as application data, expose it to users, or use it as an authentication or authorization boundary. The contract is documented in `docs/plugins/building-plugins.md` and covered at the `defineToolPlugin` factory boundary in `src/plugin-sdk/tool-plugin.test.ts`; the existing agent-context test covers runtime propagation.

## User Impact

Run-mode subagent completion no longer waits for the browser service to close every tracked tab before MCP retirement and completion delivery begin. A successor turn can start its non-browser work immediately and its browser work is admitted after the old cleanup gate releases, preserving tab safety. App-view MCP leases continue to defer retirement until their release path completes.

## Evidence

Branch-attributable CI repair:

- `check-test-types` previously failed at `src/agents/subagent-registry-lifecycle.test.ts(345,18)` because the successor fixture read optional `entry.startedAt`. The fixture now uses deterministic timestamps (`1_001`), and `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile /tmp/openclaw-core-test.tsbuildinfo` exits 0.
- The previous `checks-node-compact-large-1` failure is `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-responsive.browser.test.ts`, which is unchanged by this branch. The same file failed in current-main run [29217990227](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29217990227/job/86717742399) at a separate assertion.
- The previous `checks-node-compact-small-2` failure is `test/scripts/apple-app-i18n.test.ts`, caused by the unchanged `apps/ios/Sources/Design/SettingsProTabSections.swift`. Running that exact test in a disposable checkout of the PR base (`2f756c70a65ca345df10618b2900809936012028`) reproduced the same 2 failed / 11 passed result. No UI or iOS file is changed here.

Focused branch validation:

- `src/agents/subagent-registry-lifecycle.test.ts`: 88/88 passed.
- `src/plugin-sdk/tool-plugin.test.ts`: 6/6 passed.
- `src/agents/openclaw-tools.plugin-context.test.ts`: 20/20 passed.
- `extensions/browser/src/browser/session-tab-registry.test.ts`: 13/13 passed.
- `extensions/browser/src/browser-tool.test.ts`: 91/91 passed.
- `src/browser-lifecycle-cleanup.test.ts`: 4/4 passed.
- `oxfmt --check`, targeted `run-oxlint.mjs`, docs formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. Fresh Codex autoreview reported no accepted/actionable findings.
- `node scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs --check` reports the same pre-existing budget failure on base and branch (`public deprecated exports 3284 > 3279`, `conversation-runtime 4 > 0`, `channel-pairing 1 > 0`); this change does not alter the inventory.

Redacted runtime fallback evidence (local in-process runtime, no secrets or transcript):

```text
[runtime-proof/lifecycle] {"provider":"local-runtime-fallback","run":"old","session":"agent:…:child","events":["browser-cleanup-blocked","mcp-retirement-started","completion-announcement-started","completion-returned-before-browser-release","browser-cleanup-released"]}
[runtime-proof/browser] {"provider":"local-runtime-fallback","session":"agent:…:child","events":["browser-close-blocked","browser-close-released","successor-browser-access-resumed"]}
```

These are complementary deterministic barriers through the actual lifecycle controller and browser session registry, with the close/announce seams blocked inside the tests. The first proves completion proceeds before browser release; the second proves successor browser access resumes only after the exclusive cleanup gate releases. Identifiers are redacted. A browser-capable remote lease was not retained because the available DigitalOcean provider is SSH-only and its bootstrap was slower than the local fallback; AWS and Hetzner browser lanes were unavailable in this environment. The DigitalOcean attempt used provider `digitalocean`, lease `cbx_16823554cf26`, and was aborted before any runtime command; authenticated lease listing was empty afterward.

The remaining proof gap is a remote user-path run with a real browser service and captured completion/successor-turn timestamps. The source-level barriers and focused regression tests are present, but this environment could not produce that remote artifact without a slower or unavailable provider.

target.title: fix(whatsapp): add chunk-idle timeout to inbound media download
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where WhatsApp inbound media downloads that stall after Baileys returns a stream (headers/start ok, then no further chunks) would block `downloadInboundMedia` forever via `saveMediaStream`'s unbounded `for await`, so inbound dispatch never produces an agent reply for that message.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Wrap the Baileys AsyncIterable with a local per-chunk idle race (production default `30_000` ms), matching Telegram's download idle floor and the LINE channel pattern (open `#86873`, different owner).
- On timeout, reject with `WhatsAppInboundMediaTimeoutError`, call `iterator.return()` so Node Readable streams are destroyed, and silence the losing `next()` to avoid `unhandledRejection`.
- Tests may pass a short `chunkTimeoutMs`; production omits it and uses the 30s floor (proven with fake timers).
- Does **not** change core `saveMediaStream` / `src/media/store.ts` (avoids competing with LINE `#86873`).
- Timeout error class stays module-private (knip unused-export gate).

No new config/env surface.

## User Impact

**Before:** A stalled WhatsApp media body could hang inbound handling for that message indefinitely.

**After:** Idle streams fail closed after 30s with a clear timeout error so the monitor loop can continue.

## Evidence

Head: `2de7b8c91e1ed785a490369117ad51915e6ea6d2`

### Executable negative control + wrap proof

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/whatsapp/src/inbound/media.node.test.ts -- --run -t "chunk-idle|negative" --reporter=verbose
```

```text
[whatsapp media idle negative control] outcome=still-pending wait_ms=150 without_idle_wrap=true
[whatsapp media idle proof] timed_out=true elapsed_ms=53 chunkTimeoutMs=50 production_ms=30000
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  5 passed | 11 skipped (16)
```

## Real behavior proof

Production `downloadInboundMedia` → real `saveMediaStream` (no media-store mock) with a stalled Baileys AsyncIterable.

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/whatsapp/src/inbound/media.idle.proof.test.ts -- --run --reporter=verbose
```

```text
[whatsapp media idle production proof] timed_out=true elapsed_ms=57 real_saveMediaStream=true chunkTimeoutMs=50
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed (1)
```

- **Canonical path:** inbound media download → per-chunk idle wrap → Plugin SDK `saveMediaStream`.
- **Boundary:** real media store write path; only Baileys download is stubbed to return a never-yielding stream.
- **CI note:** `checks-node-compact-small-1` readdirSync flake and OpenClawKit dead-code job are unrelated to this surface.

AI-assisted.

target.title: fix(agents): terminate agent run on critical loop detection instead of continuing indefinitely
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Critical loop detection correctly blocks a stuck tool (`deniedReason: "tool-loop"`, `action=block`), but the blocked result was returned as an ordinary tool result. The agent kept issuing provider turns and re-calling the same tool for hours (#106231).

## Why This Change Was Made

ClawSweeper Rank-up on the previous abort-helper tip required the **canonical agent-core termination contracts** instead of `abortRun` at the embedded-run boundary (which records synthetic `stopReason: "aborted"` and can cancel sibling tools in mixed batches).

Dual-layer stop:

1. **Per-result** `terminate: true` on critical tool-loop blocked results → `shouldTerminateToolBatch` stops single/all-veto batches.
2. **Post-turn** `shouldStopAfterTurn` in `createAgentSession` → stops **mixed** batches when any finalized result has `deniedReason: "tool-loop"`.

Plugin / approval vetoes stay non-terminating.

## User Impact

- Critical tool loops terminate the agent run instead of burning tokens indefinitely.
- Mixed parallel batches complete non-loop tools, then stop before the next provider turn.
- Non-loop blocks unchanged.
- Terminal outcome follows normal loop completion (not a synthetic aborted assistant message from embedded `abortRun`).

## Evidence

**Head SHA:** `59977a726886274d04a036be59c7392972d67db9` (rebuilt from current `main`; replaces prior `critical-tool-loop-abort` approach)

**Patch quality:** platinum-shaped — 6 files, +232/−1 net, single owner boundary, no speculative exports, clean compare vs main.

| Rank-up | Status |
|---|---|
| Replace embedded abort with terminate + post-turn contracts | done |
| Cover single-tool + mixed-batch | done (`agent-loop.test.ts`, `blocked-result.test.ts`) |
| e2e asserts `terminate: true` on tool-loop blocks | done |
| Real-runtime transcript (no next provider turn; no unintended aborted entry) | **pending L3** — need live agent credentials/run |

### Commands (green locally)

```text
$ node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check <touched 6 files>
All matched files use the correct format.

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/agent-core/src/agent-loop.test.ts -t "critical|shouldStopAfterTurn|mixed batch"
✓ mixed batch shouldStopAfterTurn
✓ Agent.prompt single critical terminate
Tests  2 passed | 25 skipped

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/agent-core/src/agent-loop.test.ts src/agents/agent-tools.before-tool-call.blocked-result.test.ts
Test Files  2 shards passed (4 + 27)

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs --config test/vitest/vitest.e2e.config.ts src/agents/agent-tools.before-tool-call.e2e.test.ts -t "loop detection"
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests  38 passed | 45 skipped
```

### Before / after (contract)

| Case | BEFORE | AFTER |
|---|---|---|
| Critical tool-loop block (single tool) | result returned; model continues | `terminate: true` → batch terminates; no next provider turn |
| Critical tool-loop in mixed batch | continue if not every result terminates | `shouldStopAfterTurn` stops after turn |
| Other blocked reasons | unchanged | unchanged (no `terminate`) |

Fixes #106231

## Agent Transcript

- Cursor session: rebuild #106297 onto main using ClawSweeper-recommended terminate + shouldStopAfterTurn path.

target.title: fix(cron): drop plain-text format from announce delivery footer
target.body:
Closes #106430

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where isolated cron jobs with `delivery: announce` (and no message tool) append a footer that says **Return your response as plain text**, which some models (notably Qwen) obey by writing tool-like tags as plain text instead of making API-level tool calls. Other models ignore the instruction, so the bug is easy to miss.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace the format-constraining plain-text clause with neutral automatic-delivery guidance: **Your response will be delivered automatically.** This keeps the auto-delivery contract without telling models to suppress structured tool use.

Fix quality: compatibility — string-only prompt change on the non-message-tool announce path; no config/API/schema change. Performance — no hot-path cost. Usability — clearer delivery notice. Security — no trust-boundary change.

Note: open PR #106527 targets the same issue with a slightly different residual wording (`Return your response; …`). This PR follows ClawSweeper’s recommended neutral phrasing and drops the format instruction entirely.

## User Impact

Isolated announce cron runs can use non-message tools without a prompt footer that steers weaker models away from real tool calls. Automatic delivery of the final reply still works as before.

## Evidence

Verification host: local macOS (Crabbox bypass)

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/isolated-agent/run.message-tool-policy.test.ts
# Test Files  1 passed (1)
# Tests  56 passed (56)

pnpm exec oxfmt --check src/cron/isolated-agent/run.ts src/cron/isolated-agent/run.message-tool-policy.test.ts
# All matched files use the correct format.

git diff --check  # clean
node --import tsx scripts/check-ts-max-loc.ts --base origin/main -- src/cron/isolated-agent/run.ts
# TypeScript LOC ratchet: checked 1 changed production files. (flat)

pnpm check:changed  # partial: conflict markers, LOC, format, SDK baseline, package patches, typecheck core OK;
# typecheck core tests exceeded closeout budget (~47m still running) → stopped; focused surface proof above covers this string-only change.
```

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: Isolated announce delivery footer no longer instructs models to answer “as plain text,” which was suppressing API tool calls for some models.
- Environment: local macOS, OpenClaw checkout at `main` + this patch (`76d63df2f`), Node-driven focused Vitest via `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs`.
- Current-main contrast: `appendCronDeliveryInstruction` (non-message-tool path) still emits `Return your response as plain text; it will be delivered automatically. …` on `origin/main`. Focused tests on main require that exact substring when announce delivery is requested without the message tool.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:
  1. Inspect `src/cron/isolated-agent/run.ts` non-message-tool branch of `appendCronDeliveryInstruction`.
  2. Run `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/isolated-agent/run.message-tool-policy.test.ts`.
- Evidence after fix: Production string is `Your response will be delivered automatically. …`. Tests assert that substring is present, assert `as plain text` is absent on the non-message-tool announce path, and assert the delivery footer is still omitted when delivery is not requested. Suite result: **56/56 passed**.
- Control check: Message-tool announce path wording is unchanged (`Use the message tool… final plain-text reply will be delivered automatically`). Only the no-message-tool footer lost the format constraint. Delivery-not-requested case still has no auto-delivery footer.
- Observed result after fix: Prompt construction for announce + toolsAllow without `message` no longer contains format-constraining “as plain text” language while still stating automatic delivery.
- What was not tested: Live Qwen (or other model) tool-call turn against a real announce cron job. ClawSweeper accepted source-level repro for this issue; live model behavior was not independently re-run here.

## AI disclosure

This fix was authored with AI assistance (Grok). Human reviewer should still treat ClawSweeper guidance and the focused test output as the primary review anchors.

target.title: fix(exec): memoize duplicate auto-review verdicts
target.body:
AI-assisted: yes. I reviewed the exec approval path and understand the authorization boundary changed by this patch.

## What Problem This Solves

Addresses #102249.

The model-backed exec auto-reviewer pays for a fresh reviewer completion whenever the same ask-requiring gateway request is reviewed again. Retry and polling loops can therefore turn N identical reviews into N paid model calls even though the reviewer runs deterministically at temperature 0.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add a bounded per-reviewer-instance memo with deliberately narrow reuse semantics:

- cache only completed low-risk `allow-once` decisions for `host=gateway`;
- require a non-empty canonical gateway `resolvedPath` before caching;
- key command, argv, resolved executable, cwd, environment keys, reason, analysis, and agent context;
- never cache node-host requests, `ask`, timeout, unavailable-model, completion-error, or other fallback outcomes;
- cap the memo at 128 entries.

Node-host reuse was explicitly removed after review because its current prepare protocol does not expose a separate canonical resolved-executable field to the reviewer. This avoids crossing node or executable authorization boundaries rather than widening the protocol in a cost-optimization PR.

## User Impact

For N byte-identical gateway requests within one reviewer instance, paid reviewer completions drop from N to 1. Changed resolved executables trigger a fresh completion, and node requests retain the existing per-call review behavior.

## Evidence

Final rebase:

- `upstream/main`: `2e6fd00871b`
- branch head: `bb95ca4b779`

Validation:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/exec-auto-reviewer.test.ts src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-node.test.ts` -> 86/86 tests passed on the final rebased head.
- `oxfmt --check` on both changed files -> passed.
- LOC ratchet and `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD` -> passed.
- The full changed-file gate passed on the prior broader code tree, including core typecheck, core-test typecheck (822.82s), lint, LOC, format, dependency, import-cycle, database-first, and security guards. The final patch removes the node-host/protocol changes that tree contained and reruns the focused tests above.

Configured provider-backed runtime proof used OpenClaw's production config validation, model/auth resolution, reviewer, and OpenAI-compatible streaming HTTP transport against a local deterministic endpoint:

| Gateway request | Cumulative real completion POSTs |
| --- | ---: |
| baseline | 1 |
| byte-identical repeat | 1 |
| changed `resolvedPath` | 2 |

Both real completion calls were `POST /v1/chat/completions` with configured bearer auth, `model=reviewer-proof`, `stream=true`, and `temperature=0`; each returned a parsed low-risk `allow-once` decision. Script SHA-256: `516b27f2f7a43cac44924104306d243796be0cc87ac91494ac207f408d9a0c2b`.

Focused invariants also prove duplicate `ask` and node-host inputs are never memoized.

Signed-off-by: Ho Lim <subhoya@gmail.com>

target.title: fix(agents): bound compaction planning worker payloads
target.body:
AI-assisted: yes. I reviewed the compaction planning and worker handoff paths, checked duplicate/open PR state for #100635, and independently reviewed and validated the branch locally.

## What Problem This Solves

Addresses #100635.

Compaction planning sanitizes private fields before worker handoff, but previously still sent full model-visible tool-result text and base64 image data through `workerData`. Large browser/command results or multimodal transcripts could therefore force multi-megabyte structured-clone work before summary-prompt truncation had a chance to help.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a planning-only projection before worker handoff:

- oversized tool-result text/content keeps a bounded UTF-16-safe sample plus omitted-character accounting;
- image blocks in user, custom, and tool-result content keep type/MIME metadata but omit base64 bytes;
- token-pressure accounting remains conservative, so chunking and pruning decisions still reflect the original payload;
- local fallback behavior and private-field sanitization remain unchanged.

Image bytes are not used by compaction's text serializer, while image token pressure is a fixed per-block estimate. Omitting only `data` therefore reduces worker cloning without changing summary text or planning pressure. The projection helper is split from worker orchestration so both implementation files stay within the repository LOC guard.

## User Impact

Long or multimodal sessions should spend less time and memory cloning redundant payloads into the compaction planning worker, reducing event-loop stall and OOM risk without changing compaction decisions or generated summary text.

target.title: fix(cron): cap trigger script tool access
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a restricted agent could create a recurring cron job with a trigger script and a `systemEvent` payload, then have that script receive the full coding tool surface. Main-session cron jobs require `systemEvent`, so the common path bypassed the creator's tool policy whenever cron triggers were enabled.

## Why This Change Was Made

The creator tool cap now applies whenever a cron job has a trigger script, in addition to isolated `agentTurn` jobs. The cap is retained on every cron payload shape, survives updates, is persisted through the cron SQLite store so it survives a gateway restart, and is passed to the headless trigger evaluator. This keeps the existing agent-turn behavior while covering main-session system events and command payloads.

Distinct from #12736, which concerns global cron deny policy; #97317 and #101349, which concern isolated agent-turn defaults; and #41484, which concerns elevated execution scope.

## User Impact

Agents restricted to a small tool set can use cron triggers without acquiring shell, exec, or patch capabilities beyond that set. Existing unrestricted operator-created cron jobs continue to work with their configured policy.

## Rebase onto current main

This branch was rebased onto current `main`. Three things needed re-expressing against main's current code, none of which change the fix:

- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/cron.ts` conflicted because `main` replaced `Type.Object({...}, { additionalProperties: false })` with the `closedObject()` helper. The cap fields were re-expressed in that helper form.
- The changed-file TypeScript LOC ratchet that landed on `main` in #106387 forbids an already-oversized file from growing. `src/cron/service/jobs.ts`, `src/agents/tools/cron-tool.ts` and `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/cron.ts` are all over the limit, so the cap additions tripped the gate. Cohesive declarations were hoisted into three companion leaf modules, mirroring the existing sibling convention: `src/agents/tools/cron-tool.types.ts` (type-only), `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/cron.types.ts` (type-only wire types), and `src/cron/service/payload-merge.ts` (the cron payload merge rules the patch touches). All three source files are now back at or below their baseline line counts and the ratchet passes.
- `src/cron/store.test.ts` now uses the repo's `expectDefined` helper for indexed job access, which main's tightened unchecked index access requires.

## Evidence

- The touched suites were re-run after the rebase with `node scripts/test-projects.mjs` and all pass: 145 checks in `src/agents/tools/cron-tool.test.ts`, 199 checks across `src/cron/normalize.test.ts`, `src/cron/store.test.ts`, `src/cron/service.jobs.test.ts` and `src/cron/trigger-script.test.ts`, and 23 checks in `packages/gateway-protocol/src/cron-validators.test.ts`. 367 checks total.
- `src/cron/store.test.ts` restart-aware round-trip coverage for the `systemEvent` and `command` tool caps; both fail on the pre-persistence codec and pass here.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json` and `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json` both pass, `node --import tsx scripts/check-ts-max-loc.ts` passes, and `oxfmt --check` on the changed files is clean.
- An earlier restart cap-loss and reload proof, pinned to a previous head, is in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/104430#issuecomment-4945702410

## Real behavior proof
Behavior addressed: A cron trigger script created by a restricted caller must not receive tools the caller cannot use; a `systemEvent` main-session job with a trigger script previously kept no tool cap.
Real environment tested: The production `createCronTool` entry point (`src/agents/tools/cron-tool.ts`) driven via `tool.execute("add", ...)` on pristine main `1708faf85b` and on PR head `c891d9601bafa360c3e8faa0cfb1781a87cece7b` with the identical restricted creator (`creatorToolAllowlist: ["read", "cron"]`) creating a trigger-script `systemEvent` job; only the gateway RPC boundary was replaced to capture the params the tool sends.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: `PROOF_OUT=/tmp/proof-after.txt node_modules/.bin/tsx cron-trigger-proof.ts` (harness invokes the real cron tool `add` with `trigger.script` + `payload.kind=systemEvent`, prints the captured `cron.add` payload)
Evidence after fix:
```
# BEFORE (pristine main 1708faf85b, identical restricted-caller input)
{"kind":"systemEvent","text":"changed"}
# AFTER (this patch, head c891d9601bafa360c3e8faa0cfb1781a87cece7b, identical input)
{"kind":"systemEvent","text":"changed","toolsAllow":["read","cron"]}
```
Observed result after fix: The persisted trigger-script job carries `toolsAllow: ["read","cron"]`, capping the trigger to exactly the creator-visible tools instead of receiving the full coding tool surface.
What was not tested: No live gateway tick with a provider-backed trigger evaluation, and the full build was not run.

target.title: fix(nostr): keep profile imports as cancellable drafts
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Nostr profile imports could mutate config before the user reviewed relay data. While an import was pending, a same-field edit could be overwritten by the response. Cancel could close the form while a server-side merge still persisted.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Control UI now requests `autoMerge: false`, treats relay data as a draft, locks profile controls while importing, and aborts/invalidate imports on Cancel, disconnect, or form replacement. Late responses cannot update a hidden or newer form. Explicit **Save & Publish** remains the write path.

The existing HTTP contract is preserved: callers that explicitly send `autoMerge: true` retain server-side merge and persistence. Only the Control UI opts into draft mode.

## User Impact

Imported values fill the open form for review. Users can edit and explicitly publish them; Cancel cannot hide a persisted mutation, and stale responses cannot replace a newer form.

## Evidence

### Real Control UI + relay/browser proof

A standalone Chromium run drove the actual Control UI. Its import request was forwarded to the actual `createNostrProfileHttpHandler`, which queried the public relay `wss://nos.lol`. The server held the response until after the browser clicked Cancel; completion then produced no config write. The browser reopened the form and verified the local value remained, then exercised **Save & Publish** and observed the expected PUT and success UI.

target.title: fix(subagents): credit requester-consumed descendant completions
target.body:
## Summary

This PR fixes a lifecycle/delivery accounting gap for background and cron-owned subagent trees: when a requester actually consumes completed descendant subagent output, the descendant run is now durably credited as delivered instead of later being finalized as failed/suspended solely because no separate visible delivery event occurred.

## What Problem This Solves

Requester-owned subagent trees can legitimately consume descendant output without sending a separate descendant-visible delivery event. This is common for cron/background flows where a parent/requester gathers frozen child output, composes its own result, and then delivers that requester result outward. Before this PR, the descendant completion could remain delivery-unproven even though its output had already been consumed by the requester. Later cleanup/finalization could then classify that descendant as failed or suspended, producing delivery state that did not match real behavior. This PR gives the registry an explicit durable signal for that case: requester consumption is delivery evidence only for the exact descendant runs that were consumed, under the matching requester session/run-start window, when the requester path adopts descendant fallback output, so the consumed descendant rows do not later announce or finalize as pending just because the final outward send fails.

## User Impact / Intended Outcome

When OpenClaw can prove that a requester consumed descendant subagent output, the matching descendant run receives durable delivery credit:
- `delivery.status` is set to `"delivered"` for the matched descendant completion;
- requester-consumption metadata is persisted with the run/delivery state;
- cleanup/finalize treats `delivery.status === "delivered"` as completed delivery proof;
- normal visible-delivery paths remain required for completions that were not consumed by a requester.
The matching is intentionally narrow. Credit is only applied when all of these are true:
- the consumed run IDs are explicit;
- the requester session key matches;
- the requester run-start window matches the consuming requester run;
- the consumption kind is known;
- cron fallback credit happens when cron adopts explicit descendant fallback output for the requester result;
- nested subagent announcement credit only covers direct child run IDs that were actually included in the requester-consumed output.

This PR keeps the delivery model explicit:
- if a descendant result was visibly delivered, it is delivered;
- if a requester consumed the descendant output because cron adopted it as the requester result, the descendant is delivered by requester consumption;
- if neither happened, failure/suspension handling still applies.

## Linked Context

- Related issue: #92433 — subagent completion can be silently dropped when an announce handoff reaches a requester transcript but the requester run ends before consuming it. This PR addresses the adjacent durable-accounting problem for completions that *are* consumed by a requester.
- Related issue: #67777 — subagent completion delivery can be lost on direct-announce timeout, drain, or orphan prune. This PR does not implement the full durable inbox/spool requested there, but it narrows one delivery-accounting gap by recording proven requester consumption.
- Related issue: #86537 — suspended final delivery can expire and discard a pending subagent completion. This PR keeps requester-consumed completions from remaining indistinguishable from undelivered completions in finalization state.
- Related issue: #90299 — subagent lifecycle state can report lost active execution context while still surfacing child output. This PR contributes to lifecycle/state consistency when descendant output is actually consumed.
- Related PR: #92934 — required assistant acknowledgement for completion wake handoffs, so transcript commit alone is not treated as requester consumption. This PR complements that by adding durable credit for explicit consumed descendant run IDs.
- Related PR: #35080 — deterministic subagent announce delivery with descendant gating. This PR builds on that direction by making consumed descendant accounting durable.
- Related PR: #44205 — stale descendant cron fallback summaries. This PR keeps the same stale-vs-current discipline for requester-consumed descendant credit.
- Related PR: #95604 — Discord subagent progress feedback. This PR is not a Discord UI change, but accurate delivered/failed lifecycle state is useful to progress/failure-marker consumers.
No exact existing issue/PR was found for `markDescendantCompletionConsumedByRequester` or this exact requester-consumed credit mechanism, so this PR should stand as the focused implementation thread for that behavior.

## What Changes

When OpenClaw can prove that a requester consumed descendant subagent output, the matching descendant run receives durable delivery credit:
- `delivery.status` is set to `"delivered"` for the matched descendant completion;
- requester-consumption metadata is persisted with the run/delivery state;
- cleanup/finalize treats `delivery.status === "delivered"` as completed delivery proof;
- normal visible-delivery paths remain required for completions that were not consumed by a requester.
The matching is intentionally narrow. Credit is only applied when all of these are true:
- the consumed run IDs are explicit;
- the requester session key matches;
- the requester run-start window matches the consuming requester run;
- the consumption kind is known;
- cron fallback credit happens when cron adopts explicit descendant fallback output for the requester result;
- nested subagent announcement credit only covers direct child run IDs that were actually included in the requester-consumed output.

## Implementation Notes

Core registry/runtime changes:
- Adds requester-consumed delivery metadata to subagent registry/delivery state.
- Adds a registry operation for marking descendant completions consumed by requester.
- Persists/restores the new delivery fields.
- Exposes the new runtime operation through the existing registry runtime shims.
Main files:
- `src/agents/subagent-registry-consumption.ts`
  - Implements durable requester-consumption credit.
  - Matches by requester session, explicit run IDs, and run-start window.
  - Records requester-consumption metadata and persists the updated run state.
- `src/agents/subagent-registry.types.ts`
  - Adds delivery/requester-consumption state fields.
- `src/agents/subagent-delivery-state.ts`
  - Persists and restores the new delivery fields.
- `src/agents/subagent-registry.ts`
- `src/agents/subagent-registry-runtime.ts`
- `src/agents/subagent-announce.registry.runtime.ts`
- `src/cron/isolated-agent/delivery-subagent-registry.runtime.ts`
  - Wires the new registry operation through runtime boundaries.
Requester-consumption paths:
- `src/cron/isolated-agent/subagent-followup.ts`
  - Reads completed descendant fallback replies and returns both formatted fallback text and the consumed descendant run IDs.
- `src/cron/isolated-agent/delivery-dispatch.ts`
  - Applies cron fallback consumption credit when cron adopts explicit descendant fallback output, before the final outbound send.
- `src/agents/subagent-announce.ts`
  - Credits nested/direct child completions when their output is included in the requester-consumed announcement/wake result.
  - Uses the same latest-child dedupe input for rendering and consumed-run credit so stale child rows are not credited.
- `src/agents/subagent-announce-output.ts`
  - Keeps latest-child dedupe reusable while preserving caller-specific fields such as `runId`.

## Tests / Verification

Coverage added or extended for:
- positive requester-consumed descendant credit;
- no credit for mismatched requester session;
- no credit outside the requester run-start window;
- no credit without explicit consumed run IDs;
- persisted/restored requester-consumption delivery fields;
- cron fallback credit only after successful outbound delivery;
- cleanup/finalize treating `delivery.status === "delivered"` as proof;
- nested/direct child announcement credit;
- stale-vs-current child dedupe, including a negative assertion that stale child run IDs are not credited when stale output is not rendered.
Primary test files:
- `src/agents/subagent-registry-consumption.test.ts`
- `src/agents/subagent-delivery-state.test.ts`
- `src/agents/subagent-registry-completion.test.ts`
- `src/agents/subagent-registry.lifecycle-retry-grace.e2e.test.ts`
- `src/agents/subagent-announce.format.e2e.test.ts`

target.title: fix(tools-manager): use BigInt for lossless Content-Length comparison
target.body:
## Summary
Replace `Number()` + `isSafeInteger` with `BigInt()` for lossless Content-Length comparison in `downloadFile`.

## What Problem This Solves
`Number()` can lose precision when parsing large integer strings (≥16 digits). The existing `CONTENT_LENGTH_RE` regex `/^\d+$/` matches arbitrarily long digit strings with no upper bound, but `Number("9007199254740993")` returns `9007199254740992` — a different value.

Although `isSafeInteger` catches most precision-loss cases (any value that rounds above `MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`), relying on `Number()` for integer comparison is fragile. A Content-Length string of 20+ digits like `"99999999999999999999"` becomes `100000000000000000000` through `Number()` — completely wrong.

In practice `MAX_ARCHIVE_BYTES` is 100 MB (~10⁸), so any oversized Content-Length is caught by the numeric comparison long before precision becomes an issue. This is a **correctness hardening** — using the right tool (`BigInt`) for integer comparison so the code is obviously correct at all scales.

**Code evidence**: in `src/agents/utils/tools-manager.ts:187-188`, the current code parses Content-Length through `Number()` which is not guaranteed lossless for arbitrary-length digit strings.

## Root Cause
The code was written using `Number()` for integer parsing, which is lossy for values beyond 2⁵³ − 1 (`Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` = 9,007,199,254,740,991). The `isSafeInteger` guard partially mitigates this but:
1. It rejects values for the wrong reason (precision loss vs size cap)
2. The error message says "exceeds byte limit" when actually the value can't be accurately parsed
3. It relies on an indirect property (safe integer vs range check) rather than comparing the value directly

## Why This Fix
**Chosen approach**: `BigInt(contentLength) > BigInt(maxBytes)` — one-line replacement.

- **Correct**: `BigInt` preserves the exact integer from any digit string
- **Simpler**: replaces two conditions (`!isSafeInteger || > maxBytes`) with one (`> maxBytes`)
- **Proven**: `BigInt` is already used elsewhere in the codebase (`src/infra/kysely-sync.ts` etc.)
- **Minimal**: 2 lines removed, 1 line added

Alternatives considered:
- String length pre-check: avoids the problem but is ad-hoc
- `BigInt` + fallback: unnecessary — `BigInt` is well-supported in Node 22

## User Impact
No user-visible change. The existing behavior was already correct for all practical Content-Length values (≤ a few GB). This fix hardens the code against theoretically large Content-Length headers and makes the intent clearer.

## Evidence
- **Before (Number() approach)**: `Number("9007199254740993")` → `9007199254740992` (precision LOST). `Number("99999999999999999999")` → `100000000000000000000` (massively wrong). ❌ FAIL
- **After (BigInt() approach)**: `BigInt("9007199254740993")` → `9007199254740993n` (exact). `BigInt("99999999999999999999")` → `99999999999999999999n` (exact). ✓ PASS

## Real Behavior Proof

### Before (Number() approach — precision loss)
```bash
$ node --import tsx proof.mjs
============================================================
Content-Length precision loss demonstration
============================================================
Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER = 9007199254740991

--- Case 1: Large Content-Length (above MAX_SAFE_INTEGER) ---
Content-Length header: "9007199254740993"
Number("9007199254740993") = 9007199254740992
Actual BigInt value : 9007199254740993
Precision preserved?  : NO — LOST!

Old code (Number + isSafeInteger):
  declaredBytes = Number("9007199254740993") = 9007199254740992
  isSafeInteger(9007199254740992) = false
  => REJECT (declaredBytes=9007199254740992, reason="exceeds cap or not safe integer")

--- Case 3: 20-digit Content-Length ---
Number("99999999999999999999") = 100000000000000000000
Number result accurate?  NO — massively wrong!

FAIL: Number() lost precision on Content-Length '9007199254740993'
FAIL: Number() returned wrong value for 20-digit Content-Length
```

### After (BigInt() comparison — exact)
```bash
$ node --import tsx proof.mjs
--- Case 1: Large Content-Length (above MAX_SAFE_INTEGER) ---
New code (BigInt comparison):
  BigInt("9007199254740993") = 9007199254740993n
  9007199254740993n > 10n = true
  => REJECT (reason="exceeds cap")

--- Case 2: Normal Content-Length (within safe range) ---
Old: ACCEPT  |  New: ACCEPT

PASS: BigInt() preserves exact value: 9007199254740993n
```

## Tests and Validation
- `pnpm check` passed
- `vitest run src/agents/utils/tools-manager.test.ts` — 18 tests passed (2 new: large Content-Length rejection)
- Added regression test: "rejects downloads with large Content-Length that would lose precision with Number()"
